newsitem.title: SPAIN: Endesa earnings seen brighter in 1998 than 1997.
newsitem.headline: Endesa earnings seen brighter in 1998 than 1997.

text.p: After a fall of eight percent in Endesa's first quarter earnings, full 1997 figures should be flat or slightly higher than in 1996, with a much better performance expected in 1998, analysts said on Friday.
But this is not expected negatively to affect the government's plans to privatise up to a 35 percent of the electricity firm in the second half of this year.
"Despite forecasts for flat 1997 results, the privatisation should be very sucessful," a Spanish analyst said.

On Thursday Endesa posted a fall of 8.03 percent in attributable profit to 39.21 billion pesetas ($272.5 million) in the first quarter, although operating income climbed to 309.17 billion pesetas from 212.72 billion the year-earlier quarter.
Sales to final clients fell 0.4 percent amid a total sector decline in demand of 1.9 percent.
But results were well-received, with the shares still near an all-time high of 10,910 pesetas hit on Tuesday.
Ignacio Montejo, head of research at Merrill Lynch Espana said Endesa had performed well in a difficult scenario.
"The results are good in the context, with the eight percent fall (in earnings) due to a series of exceptional circumstances," he said.
Results were dulled by higher costs due to lower rainfall than in the previous year, lower demand for electricity after a comparatively mild winter and a tariff cut of three percent.
Added to this the electricity giant had much greater depreciation charges due to a change in the law last year allowing firms to update the value of fixed assets in order to get tax benefits.
Depreciation rose by 24.89 billion pesetas in the first quarter of which 8.58 billion corresponded to the asset revaluation programme, Endesa said.
Operating income was boosted by the full incorporation of regional utilities Fecsa and Sevillana, of which Endesa bought a further stake last year to own 75 percent of each.
Excluding this, the tariff cut and lower demand would have seen a four percent decline at the operating level.
However these elements were one-offs, analysts said, and although net earnings in 1997 as a whole are not expected to be spectacular, 1998 should see better things.

"Endesa has the capacity to reduce its debt levels because it has a high cash flow, while at the same time it should be able to cut costs overall and become more efficient," Merrill Lynch's Montejo said.
Analysts are forecasting 1997 earnings at around 166 to 181 billion pesetas, while 1998 should see growth of about 10 percent on top of that figure.
